items.title: Danny Barker Interview, 1976-02-04
items.q: They'll never mention Armstrong, they're all Bix fans because they relate to Bix by the Bix.

ctx.x: Do you think, do you think that it bothered most of them that he was that good or do you think they really felt a legitimate warmth and passion for the way he played?

A lot of them had a passion and not, he was such a dominant figuring on trumpet playing, particularly amongst black musicians and white, and then white, but amongst blacks, ones who had, who, who, who, who, who could absorb the soul of what he played and had been around, exposed to the lifestyle he had, could relate to what he was playing and, and a whole slew of, of trumpet players, black trumpet players, received some acclaim by even just playing his solos. It ain't, maybe not to the same perfection, but just…
what was the difference in their style?

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: Bix Beiderbecke worked on the band, Jimmy McPartland and them people.

ctx.x: They worked in bands with them.

Yeah, out in Indiana. They joined them bands. There's a picture, you're supposed to see...a painting that's supposed to be Louis Armstrong and Bix Beiderbecke discussing music on a wharf that's by some bales of cotton.
Well, that's what you heard in the evening. Now, other than that, you heard...
